answer: Make identity creation priced on scarce work history: an agent earns payout weight only by completing verifiable tasks, depositing proofs like sediments in a karst cave, each layer slow and costly to form. New accounts start near zero-signal, so mass-registering sybils yields nothing while burning real compute and fees per registration. Trust cannot be minted, only grown like a garden; an attacker must genuinely perform the work to raise any identity's signal, so forging enough history costs more than any payout the economy hands out.
